text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Charles Kuria Wamwere, brother to Kenyan dissident Koigi wa Wamwere, and former army captain Geoffrey Njuguna Ngengi -- serving a four-year jail term each for robbery -- are granted bail on medical grounds.
- Farmers in the marginal areas of Eastern Province face serious food shortages following failure of rains.

- The Kenyan civil service is plagued by low morale as a result of corruption, nepotism, tribalism and poor remuneration and benefits for its members, committee appointed by President Daniel arap Moi reports.
- Fresh controversy erupts over the government's January 31 deadline for the acquisition of new generation national identity cards.
- Business at Kencom House Nairobi, headquarters of Kenya Commercial Bank, comes to a standstill for several hours following a bomb scare.
- Kenya's third international airport in Eldoret is now complete and will be handed over to the government in a few days.
- FORD-Kenya first vice-chairman James Orengo is set to challenge incumbent party chairman Michael Kijana Wamalwa for the party leadership.
